messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate and streaming disconnects on `svc-inference-east-prod` (streaming routes). Metric link: https://metrics.redwood/internal/streams?alert=stream-5xx

Aisha: seeing spikes starting ~14:02 UTC, 5xx up to ~7% on streaming endpoints, non-streaming endpoints look mostly fine. Clients reporting chunked encoding errors and early connection closes.

Tom: on it. Do we have nginx/ingress logs showing `upstream prematurely closed connection` or `client prematurely closed connection`?

Aisha: past 10m raw from ingress (tail):
```
[14:05:12] "POST /v1/stream" 502 0 "-" "upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream"
[14:06:01] "POST /v1/stream" 504 0 "-" "upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream"
[14:07:34] "POST /v1/stream" 200 0 "-" "client closed connection"
```

Priya: customers on Dedicated are seeing higher error rates too, getting paging messages from SRE oncalls. We need customer impact triage (who, routes, retries).

James: adding logs from runtime workers, looks like backend inference workers are returning partial chunks then resetting TCP: `write() failed: Broken pipe` and `connection reset by peer`. Also saw `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` then socket closed mid-stream.

Aisha: hypothesis: something in the streaming path (chunked transfer, keepalive, proxy buffer) causing premature socket closes. Could be connection pooling to runtime or runtime hitting limit and forcibly closing.

Tom: quick mitigations we can try in parallel:
- increase upstream read timeout on ingress (nginx) from 60s -> 120s for streaming routes
- temporarily disable streaming for specific high-impact customers (fall back to non-streaming endpoint)
- scale up inference pool for east-prod by +30% to reduce queueing
- toggle worker `stream_chunk_ms` down to reduce time between chunks

Priya: I'm drafting a customer-facing note for impacted users and will call top 3 accounts. Which ones have highest errors?

Aisha: top impacted api-keys: acct-42, acct-178, acct-901 (IDs masked). Errors concentrated on `/v1/stream` with long-lived streams > 30s.

infra-bot: Scaling action initiated: adding 4 inference instances to `east-prod-pool-1` (expected +25% capacity).

Tom: I'm applying an ingress timeout change now to a single canary host for streaming routes. Will monitor.

Aisha: applying temporary route config to map `acct-42` and `acct-178` to `v1/generate` (non-streaming) so they get blocking responses instead of streaming. Patching policy now.

James: restarting a subset of runtime workers to flush possible bad connections. Doing a rolling restart group-by-group to avoid total outage.

(5m pass)

Aisha: after scaling + timeout increase + routing 2 customers to non-streaming, 5xx dropped from 7% -> 1.8% overall but some spikes remain. Streaming disconnects still ~0.5% for long sessions.

Tom: can we capture a full tcpdump for a failing session? Need to see if chunk boundaries are being sent and then reset. If proxy sends `Connection: keep-alive` but backend closes early that's likely runtime.

James: captured sample pcap and pulled raw bytes. Observed: chunked chunks sent, then backend sends RST after ~2-3 chunks with no error payload.

Priya: notified principal customers: sent note and offered mitigation steps (switch to non-streaming endpoint, increase retries). Next: prepare official status update.

Aisha: hypothesis 2: KV cache eviction combined with a hot path causing long compute + blocked IO leads to worker OOM or forced close. Checking runtime memory/GC logs.

James: runtime GC spikes correlate with 14:04-14:08 window. Some workers showing 85-95% memory and then `OOM-killer` like logs preceding socket close. Found `alloc failed: could not allocate` in one worker log.

Tom: OK that points to runtime resource exhaustion. Immediate mitigation: reduce `max_concurrent_streams` per worker from 32 -> 12, and reduce batch size for streaming inference. That will reduce throughput but keep connections healthy.

infra-bot: Config change pushed: `max_concurrent_streams=12` for `east-prod` streaming runtime (gradual rollout).

Aisha: rolling changes applied. Observing per-worker stream counts fall and mem pressure easing. 5xxs now down to 0.6% and streaming disconnects trending down.

Tom: good. I'm going to leave a handoff — I need to jump to another page. James, can you own the rest of the live debugging and stay on thread? Priya, continue customer comms and update status page.

James: taking over. Next steps:
- validate no regressions for non-streaming endpoints
- run synthetic long-streams (45m) to ensure stability
- collect full runtime heap dumps from 2 affected workers for postmortem
- investigate why GC/alloc spikes happened (regression in model code or memory leak after last release?)

Priya: status update drafted and posted to status.redwood: "Investigating elevated streaming errors; mitigation in place — scaling and runtime config changes. Some customers temporarily on non-streaming endpoints. No data loss reported. Follow-up postmortem planned."

(15m later)

James: synthetic long stream tests at 14:40 show stable runs for 30m+ with new config. Heap dumps saved to: s3://redwood-infra/incident-dumps/1773005555/

Aisha: we should roll back customer reroutes once stable. Plan: keep `max_concurrent_streams=12` for next 24h, monitor error budget, then gradually raise. Also add an alert for runtime memory >80% per-worker.

Tom: postmortem owners assigned: James (runtime), Aisha (ingress and routing), Priya (customer comms). Action items: add pre-deploy memory pressure test, add synthetic streaming canary, and add circuit-breaker that detects repeated chunk RSTs and auto-fallback to non-streaming for that API key.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied. 5xx rate reduced from 7% -> 0.4%. Incident severity downgraded to P2. Follow-up ticket created: #INC-1773005555 (postmortem and action items).

Priya: I'll schedule customer follow-ups + exec summary. Notifying legal for records (no PII impacted).

James: leaving logs + heap dumps + pcap in the incident folder. Will run deeper mem profiler tomorrow. If anything resurfaces ping me directly.

Tom: thanks team — leaving this in James' hands.

Aisha: thanks. Closing live ops channel in 30m unless spikes reappear.

(End of thread)
